headline: Bitcoin bounces 2.39% on the day while still down on the week, and every major sits under its 200-day line
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles every other question before you ask it. All seven majors in this tape, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA, are below their 200-day moving averages. No golden crosses anywhere. That's a market still working through a downtrend, not one asset lagging behind six others in an uptrend. Bitcoin sits 48.4% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 60.4% from its high, and ADA is the worst of the group at 81.9% off. When the whole board agrees like this, the story is the trend, not any single candle.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, because it doesn't match the trend's mood. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is 53.5, ETH's is 55.9, BNB's is 58.7, all comfortably neutral-to-firm, not oversold, not stretched. But layer in the timeframes and you get a genuine split: Bitcoin is up 2.39% on the day, down 0.81% over the past week, and up 1.19% over the past month. That's a bounce inside a flat-to-slightly-positive month, sitting inside a year-long downtrend. Bitcoin's MACD is still below its signal line despite the day's green candle, so the day's move hasn't yet flipped the momentum indicator that trades on a slower clock. SOL, BNB, and DOGE do have MACD above signal, a smaller divergence worth naming: momentum turning up under assets that remain under their 200-day lines and, in SOL's case, still down 7% on the month.

Positioning adds texture. Bitcoin funding on OKX is barely alive at 0.1% annualized, about as close to free as leverage gets, and the long/short account ratio of 1.62 shows more accounts positioned long than short, but the cost of holding that long is nearly nothing. That's not a crowded, expensive trade; it's cheap and quiet. ETH funding is actually negative (-0.8% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position, an unusual tilt for an asset up 1.77% on the day. XRP and DOGE run hot by comparison, funding at 6.5% and 10.3% annualized with long/short ratios of 3.68 and 5.16, a much more one-sided, more expensive bet stacked in those two names. Liquidations over roughly the past day skewed heavily toward shorts getting squeezed across BTC ($8.8M shorts vs $1.9M longs) and ETH ($5.1M shorts vs $2.0M longs), consistent with a market that had leaned bearish into this bounce and is now paying for it.

Flows tell a quieter but firmer story. Whale wallets moved $29.0 million net off exchanges in the past 24 hours, continuing the pattern from the last two entries in the weekly series (-$439.0M and -$123.3M), though the two entries before that were sharply positive ($701.7M and $1,074.7M), so call this a recent shift rather than a settled trend. The single biggest off-exchange move was $177.0M in BTC leaving Bitstamp; the biggest onto-exchange move was $129.9M in USDT arriving at Bitfinex, tagged as stablecoin buying power. On the ETF side, BTC funds saw -$56.2M net on 14 Aug 2026, the third straight day in the same direction, for a five-session net of -$385.2M; ETH funds took in +$5.9M on 13 Aug with a five-session net of +$46.6M. So spot BTC demand from traditional finance has been leaking out over the past week while whale wallets, on net, pulled coins into cold storage, a real tension between two different pools of capital. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, sits at $306.4B, down a mild 0.59% over 30 days, not a story of dry powder building or draining hard either way.

Sentiment is the foil here, and it's worth stating plainly: the Fear & Greed gauge reads 31, Fear, sitting mid-range against its own 30-day band of 25 to 34. The crowd feels nervous while Bitcoin prints a 2.39% green day, funding stays cheap, and shorts just ate the liquidation bill. That gap between how people say they feel and what the leverage and liquidation data show is itself the reading for today: fear on the survey, a short squeeze on the tape.

What to watch from here: whether BTC's MACD actually crosses above its signal line (it hasn't yet despite the bounce), whether the five-session ETF flow flips positive after three straight negative prints, and whether the whale weekly series turns back toward inflows to exchanges the way it did two entries ago. Any one of those flipping would change today's read; none of them have yet.
